Topic 2.4: Talk About

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Talk About. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use acquired vocabulary to talk 2 lessons about self appropriately him/her/it?
2. identify themselves with people, objects and places in their environment
3. demonstrate interest to use names of people, places, and objects within the environment
4. express personal emotions, feelings, and opinions about people, places, and objects Core-Competence to be developed: Self-efficacy: learners name objects, people, and places Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to discuss various topics Digital literacy: learners interact with the audio and visual recorders as they engage in conversation Creativity and imagination: learners recreate stories 132

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use acquired vocabulary to talk 2 lessons about self appropriately him/her/it?
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use acquired vocabulary to talk 2 lessons about self appropriately him/her/it?. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify themselves with people, objects and places in their environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify themselves with people, objects and places in their environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. demonstrate interest to use names of people, places, and objects within the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate interest to use names of people, places, and objects within the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. express personal emotions, feelings, and opinions about people, places, and objects Core-Competence to be developed: Self-efficacy: learners name objects, people, and places Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to discuss various topics Digital literacy: learners interact with the audio and visual recorders as they engage in conversation Creativity and imagination: learners recreate stories 132

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Talk About using something you see at school.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Talk About.
2. Explain Talk About to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Talk About.
4. Show that you can: use acquired vocabulary to talk 2 lessons about self appropriately him/her/it?
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Talk About. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Talk About important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER
